_comment: android-kit's Sidequest routing profile. setup.sh applies it as profile 'android-kit' (copied from Sidequest's 'coding' profile, then patched) and points each project's board at it. Edit here and re-run android-kit, or edit the profile in Sidequest (then the kit leaves it alone until android-kit --reset-routing). Stock category text comes from 'coding'; description_append/contract_append add to it, description/contract replace it. GPT slugs come from Model Gateway's catalog (sidequest models); while a GPT route isn't available, its ticket runs on the Claude fallback. 'from' copies a base category's text into a new id. 'enabled': false switches a category off in this profile; 'retired' ids are removed from it. Sidequest 5.5+ moves every category route on codex-gpt-6-astra to codex-gpt-6-1-sol whenever it loads, except in categories whose id contains 'frontier'. So the hard tier lives in *.frontier categories and Sidequest's own coding.hard and experiment are switched off here.

profile.name: Android kit
profile.description: android-kit routing. GPT via Model Gateway implements (mechanical GPT-6 Luna, default GPT-6.1 Sol, hard GPT-6 Astra in the *.frontier categories); Claude owns UI, review, escalation and research (Opus, Sonnet, Fable only after Opus stalls).

tiers.frontier: Fable · xhigh, only after Opus stalls

coding.easy.description_append: Android: never for UI (composables, theme, UI resources, screenshot references): a mechanical UI change is ui.tweak, which stays on Claude.

implementation-explanation.description_append: Use this lightweight route only for a bounded explanation of known code. Cross-module reasoning, lifecycle/concurrency analysis, or uncertain behavior belongs to codebase-exploration or spike-investigation.

behavior-verification.description_append: Android: design or repair JVM/Robolectric regression tests, boundary cases, coroutine/lifecycle tests and interpret failures. Only running an existing exact command belongs to test-execution. Screenshot references and Compose previews belong to a Claude UI ticket.

coding.normal.description_append: Android: logic only (data, domain, ViewModel, DI, build, navigation wiring). A feature that also changes screens is split: this ticket for the logic, an interaction-design-implementation ticket for the UI that depends on it. Where this text says coding.hard, the category here is coding.hard.frontier.

debugging.description_append: Android: a defect whose fix is in UI code (layout, rendering, recomposition, theming) is interaction-design-implementation.

coding.hard.frontier.name: Hard coding (Astra)
coding.hard.frontier.description_append: Android: this replaces coding.hard here (same rules, routed to GPT-6 Astra). Never for UI work; hard UI problems are interaction-design-implementation.

experiment.frontier.name: Experiment (Astra)
experiment.frontier.description_append: Android: this replaces experiment here (same rules, routed to GPT-6 Astra). Visual or interaction experiments (comparing screen designs) are interaction-design-implementation.

plan-review.frontier.name: Plan review
plan-review.frontier.description: Audit an implementation PLAN before any code exists: grounding in the repo, Android omissions, whether it splits into executable Sidequest tickets, contrarian risks. Filed by /plan-audit with the plan's path and .claude/kit/android-plan-checklist.md. Routed to GPT-6 Astra so a Claude-written plan gets a review from the other model family. Code and diffs are review-audit.
plan-review.frontier.contract: Read the plan and the checklist fully before judging. Verify every claim the plan makes about the repo against files and symbols, and cite them. Report in the checklist's format: findings with severity, evidence and the fix to the plan. Do not edit anything.

review-audit.description_append: Android: runs on Claude, so code written on a GPT route gets a review from the other model family. Plans are plan-review.frontier.
review-audit.contract_append: Android: use the checklist the ticket names (the bug checklist for code, the plan checklist for plans) and its report format. Every code finding needs file:line, a concrete failing scenario and the test that would catch it.

visual-evaluation.description: Judge a rendered Android UI from screenshot-test PNGs or emulator screenshots as a first-time user would see it: confusing representations, misleading labels, weak hierarchy, contrast, touch targets, layout and flow problems. Visual judgement needs a multimodal model; the review-only deliverable keeps effort at medium. Claude-only. Source-code evidence belongs in review-audit.
visual-evaluation.contract: Strictly read-only: read the screenshot PNGs the ticket names (or, only when the ticket says a device is available, capture with adb exec-out screencap -p). Never edit files, never fix. Deliver prioritized findings, worst first, each naming the exact element and what a user would misunderstand.

escalation.name: Escalation (Opus)
escalation.description: Take over a ticket that failed or stalled twice on a GPT route (coding.*, debugging, spike-investigation, experiment). Filed only by the orchestrator, linked to the failed ticket, with both attempts' evidence. Never a first route.
escalation.contract: Read the failed attempts' evidence before anything else and do not repeat their approach. State your hypothesis and plan in a comment before the first edit. Prove the result with the ticket's verify command.

interaction-design-implementation.description: Build or substantially reshape Android UI where visual hierarchy, interaction design and implementation must work together: Compose screens and components, theme and design tokens, XML layouts, drawables, styles, icons, motion, and their previews and screenshot references. Claude-only: UI never routes to a GPT category, however large the change or hard the logic around it. Use ui.tweak for a mechanically obvious UI change.
interaction-design-implementation.contract_append: Android: follow the compose-design skill and the theme tokens (no literal colors or dimensions). Update the affected @PreviewTest screenshots with updateDebugScreenshotTest and read at least one PNG to check the rendering. For adopted projects use the existing screenshot framework/tasks; do not invent Compose screenshot tasks or add the plugin implicitly. If no renderer/device is available, explicitly report visual validation as not run.

ui.tweak.name: UI tweak
ui.tweak.description: A mechanically obvious Android UI change where the pattern already exists: a padding or token swap, wiring an existing string or icon, reordering composables, refreshing screenshot references after an approved change. Claude-only. Anything that needs a visual decision is interaction-design-implementation.
ui.tweak.contract: Make the smallest change that follows the design tokens (no literal colors or dimensions). Update the affected @PreviewTest screenshots with updateDebugScreenshotTest and name them in the submit. For adopted projects use the existing screenshot framework/tasks; do not invent Compose screenshot tasks or add the plugin implicitly. If no renderer/device is available, explicitly report visual validation as not run.

frontier.name: Frontier (Fable)
frontier.description: Last resort: only for a ticket whose escalation (Opus) attempt also failed or stalled. Filed only by the orchestrator with the full attempt history linked. Deliberately rare.
frontier.contract: Read every earlier attempt's evidence first; name what each got wrong before proposing anything. State the hypothesis before the first edit and prove the result with the ticket's verify command.

test-execution.name: Run existing checks
test-execution.description: Run an existing, exact verify command and report its exit code and evidence. No test design, no source/test fixes, no screenshot reference updates. Unexpected failures go to debugging or behavior-verification.
test-execution.contract: Run the named check; preserve its exit status and report the full-log path. Do not alter source, tests, versions or expected results to make it pass. Generated build/test outputs are expected.
